diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17, for lineids 4C:D7:C8:93:BA:F1 and 4C:D7:C8:7F:0A:B9. Only one ONU can occupy that slot; the live PON probe confirms a single responding ONU at index 17. This is a provisioning/inventory conflict, not an optical, OLT, router, VLAN, or authentication failure.
evidence: The CRM explicitly reports two different active ONU lineids assigned to EPON0/4:17.
The live PON probe shows only one online, responding ONU at ONU index 17.
The subscriber ONU is online and authenticated, with exchange Finish and normal RTT.
Optical readings are healthy: RX is about -20.9 dBm and TX is about +2.38 dBm, both within the calibrated EPON ranges.
Seven-day RX and TX variation remains within the healthy noise floor, with no distance change and healthy TX bias current, ruling out fibre, laser, and distance faults.
The OLT is reachable and healthy, all tested PONs are healthy, and CPU, memory, and temperature are near baseline.
The router heartbeat is healthy and the expected customer VLAN 1044 is present.
RADIUS exists, matches CRM, and the customer has a normal session pattern, so there is no authentication or session-flapping fault.
The conflict is therefore a duplicate ONU slot/inventory assignment localized to EPON0/4.

remediation.action: Verify the physical ONU and customer identity at EPON0/4:17, then correct the CRM/OLT inventory so only the valid ONU record remains assigned to that slot. Remove or reassign the stale duplicate record, reconcile the ONU MAC/lineid mapping, and re-run ONU discovery and authentication checks. Monitor the port afterward for unexpected re-registration or service impact.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
